history.summary: The Tilla Mandir is a large Nath-tradition temple complex in the Ram Nagar area of Ambala City (near Jagadhri Gate), dedicated to Guru Gorakhnath. One travel source (ambalaonline.in) calls it 'the largest temple of Haryana' - claim UNVERIFIED - and describes a lineage of spiritual chiefs known as Tilladheeshes. Its most distinctive feature is the Gorakhnath Dhwaj, a 108-foot-tall flag raised in honour of Guru Gorakhnath. The temple is most famous for its Mahashivratri celebrations. Coordinates are approximate: directory listings give two nearby pins about 0.8 km apart (30.386064, 76.77804 and 30.386714, 76.769719); the figure used is the one labelled 'Gate no 1 (Mukhiya Dwar) Tilla Mandir'.

town_description: Ambala is a major city in Haryana on the Punjab border, split into the twin hubs of Ambala City and Ambala Cantonment. It is one of North India's most important railway junctions, has a large military cantonment and Air Force presence, and is famous across India for its cloth and scientific-instrument markets. Tradition links the city's name to Goddess Amba (Bhawani Amba), whose ancient temple stands in the city.
